item.title: The Database Got a New User: Record Stores and Context Layers for Agents
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: the database’s main user stopped being a person, so it grew a second leg — one that holds state and provisions on demand, one that supplies context and compiles it ahead of the query. What really changed is the definition of retrieval: from a recall algorithm to an orchestration frame plus a compiled supply.

item.title: Super-agent: DeepSeek Takes Sessions Away From the User
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: the interesting claim in DeepSeek Harness’s architecture note is not its five modules — modules change with deployment. It is one sentence: sessions should be an implementation detail of the system, not a mental burden on its user. Everything below is that sentence, taken seriously. Published 2026-10-31, the note opens by telling you what it is not: an architecture discussion, not a description of shipping features.

item.title: A Decentralized, Trusted MCP Runtime: Architecture and Implementation
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: treat a tool as a content-addressed artifact, run it inside a sandbox, and keep an identity behind it — only then does “trusted” mean anything. That is the architecture; the second half of this article is the implementation. 1. The problem: an agent’s tools are black boxes# An agent’s capability is not bounded by its model.
